note: Safe methods and record sheets as structured slots, in the Safer Food Better Business structure the officer expects. Every slot is a fact the operator has to confirm. Nothing is filled in from a default: an unconfirmed slot renders as a [CONFIRM] marker, which is what the readiness check looks for.
footer: Rescore helps you prepare your own food safety records and re-rating request. It is not an inspection, it is not a guarantee of a rating, and the records are only true if your kitchen matches them.

safeMethods.title: Keeping raw and ready-to-eat food apart

slots.prompt: Which unit holds raw meat, fish or poultry, and which shelf?
slots.example: Fridge 1 under the prep table, bottom shelf

slots.prompt: Which unit holds ready-to-eat food?
slots.example: Fridge 2 by the back door

slots.prompt: Which boards and knives are used for raw food, and how are they told apart?
slots.example: Red boards, kept on the left hook

slots.prompt: If raw and ready-to-eat food are prepared on the same surface, what happens in between?
slots.example: Surface washed, sanitised and left the contact time before ready-to-eat prep

safeMethods.body: Raw meat, fish and poultry are kept in {{raw_storage_unit}}. Ready-to-eat food is kept in {{ready_storage_unit}}. Raw food is prepared using {{raw_boards}}. Where the same surface is used for both, {{prep_separation}}.
safeMethods.check: Before each service, look at each fridge and confirm nothing raw is above anything ready to eat.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Throw away any ready-to-eat food that raw food has touched or dripped onto. Clean and sanitise the surface before using it again.

safeMethods.title: Cooking food through

slots.prompt: Which dishes do you cook from raw?
slots.example: Chicken curry, lamb kebab, fried fish

slots.prompt: How do you check each one is cooked through?
slots.example: Probe the thickest part to 75 degrees C

slots.prompt: Where is the probe thermometer kept, and where are the probe wipes?
slots.example: In the drawer by the pass, wipes in the same drawer

safeMethods.body: We cook {{cooked_dishes}} from raw. Each is checked by {{cooking_check}}. The probe is kept {{probe_location}} and is wiped before and after every use.
safeMethods.check: Probe the thickest part of the first portion of each dish at the start of service and write the reading on the cooking record.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Keep cooking and check again. Do not serve until the check passes.

safeMethods.title: Chilled storage

slots.prompt: List every fridge, freezer and chilled display, with where each one stands.
slots.example: Fridge 1 under the prep table, Fridge 2 by the back door, Freezer 1 in the yard store

slots.prompt: What temperature does each chilled unit run at?
slots.example: Fridge 1 at 4 degrees C, Fridge 2 at 3 degrees C

slots.prompt: When are the chilled units checked each day?
slots.example: Opening and close

safeMethods.body: Our chilled and frozen units are {{cold_units}}. They run at {{cold_target}}. They are checked at {{cold_check_times}} and the readings are written on the temperature record for that unit.
safeMethods.check: Read each unit's own display or probe a stored item, and write the reading down.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Move the food to a working unit. Write down what you moved and when. If food has been above 8 degrees C for more than four hours, throw it away.

safeMethods.title: Cooling cooked food

slots.prompt: Which cooked dishes do you cool and keep?
slots.example: Rice, curry base, cooked chicken

slots.prompt: How do you cool them, and how fast?
slots.example: Portioned into shallow trays, uncovered on the cold bench, into the fridge within 90 minutes

safeMethods.body: We cool {{cooled_dishes}}. The method is {{cooling_method}}. Cooling is recorded on the cooling record with the time it started and the time it went in the fridge.
safeMethods.check: Check the food is cold to the centre before it goes in the fridge, and write the times down.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: If cooling took longer than the method allows, throw the food away. Do not put it back on the line.

safeMethods.title: Reheating

slots.prompt: Which dishes do you reheat?
slots.example: Curry base, cooked rice

slots.prompt: How do you check a reheated dish is hot enough?
slots.example: Probe to 75 degrees C in the centre

safeMethods.body: We reheat {{reheated_dishes}}. Each is checked by {{reheat_check}} and the reading goes on the reheating record. Food is reheated once only.
safeMethods.check: Probe the centre of the first portion and write the reading down.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Keep heating and check again. If it will not reach the temperature, throw it away.

safeMethods.title: Hot holding

slots.prompt: List every hot hold unit and where it stands.
slots.example: Bain marie on the counter, heated display by the till

slots.prompt: When is hot holding checked?
slots.example: At the start of service and every two hours after

safeMethods.body: Hot food is held in {{hot_units}} at 63 degrees C or above. Checks are made {{hot_check_times}} and written on the hot holding record.
safeMethods.check: Probe the food in each unit and write the reading down.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: If food has been below 63 degrees C for less than two hours, reheat it to 75 degrees C once or serve it within the two hours. Longer than that, throw it away.

safeMethods.title: Defrosting

slots.prompt: What do you defrost?
slots.example: Chicken thighs, fish fillets

slots.prompt: Where do you defrost it, and how long does it take?
slots.example: Covered tray on the bottom shelf of Fridge 1, overnight

safeMethods.body: We defrost {{defrost_items}}. Defrosting happens {{defrost_place}}, covered, below any ready-to-eat food, and the item is used within 24 hours of defrosting.
safeMethods.check: Feel the centre of the item. If there is still ice in the middle, it is not ready to cook.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Never refreeze food that has defrosted. Cook it or throw it away.

safeMethods.title: Cleaning as you go and the deep clean

slots.prompt: Which sanitiser do you use, and what is its contact time?
slots.example: The green spray, two minutes contact time

slots.prompt: What gets cleaned between tasks?
slots.example: Boards, knives, the prep bench and the handles

slots.prompt: Who does the deep clean and on which day?
slots.example: The owner, every Sunday after close

safeMethods.body: We use {{sanitiser}}. Between tasks we clean {{clean_as_you_go}}. The deep clean is done by {{deep_clean_owner}} and every item on the cleaning schedule has a frequency and a name against it.
safeMethods.check: At close, walk the kitchen against the cleaning schedule and sign it off.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: If something on the schedule was missed, do it before the next service and note it on the sheet.

safeMethods.title: Pest control

slots.prompt: Who is your pest control contractor, and how often do they visit?
slots.example: Named contractor, every 8 weeks

slots.prompt: What proofing is in place at doors, windows and pipework?
slots.example: Brush strip on the back door, mesh on the yard window

safeMethods.body: Pest control is by {{pest_contractor}}. Proofing in place: {{pest_proofing}}. Every visit report is kept in the pest control log.
safeMethods.check: Look for droppings, gnawing and flies at opening, and record anything you find.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Call the contractor the same day, record the call, and throw away any food that pests have reached.

safeMethods.title: Allergens

slots.prompt: Who answers allergen questions from customers?
slots.example: The owner, and the named supervisor on late shifts

slots.prompt: Which dishes have you confirmed the full ingredients for?
slots.example: Confirmed dish by dish on the allergen matrix

slots.prompt: What do you do when a customer declares an allergy?
slots.example: Clean board and knife, fresh oil where possible, the order is made first

safeMethods.body: Allergen questions are answered by {{allergen_owner}}. The allergen matrix is built from ingredients confirmed dish by dish: {{allergen_matrix_source}}. When a customer declares an allergy, {{allergen_separation}}.
safeMethods.check: Check the matrix covers every dish on the menu today. Any dish not confirmed is not sold to a customer with an allergy.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: If you are not certain what is in a dish, say so and do not sell it to that customer.
safeMethods.neverInfer: Rescore never suggests an allergen and never marks a dish free of one. A blank cell prints: confirm with the person who prepares this dish.

safeMethods.title: Suppliers and traceability

slots.prompt: Who do you buy from, and what from each?
slots.example: Named cash and carry for dry goods, named butcher for meat

slots.prompt: What do you check when a delivery arrives?
slots.example: Temperature of chilled items, date codes, packaging intact

safeMethods.body: We buy from {{suppliers}}. On delivery we check {{delivery_check}} and keep the delivery note. Invoices and delivery notes are kept in date order for traceability.
safeMethods.check: Probe one chilled item per delivery and write the reading on the delivery record.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Reject the delivery, note why on the record, and tell the supplier.

safeMethods.title: Training and supervision

slots.prompt: Who is in charge of food safety here?
slots.example: The owner

slots.prompt: Who has which food safety training, and when did they do it?
slots.example: Named staff with Level 2, with dates

slots.prompt: What does a new member of staff get on their first day?
slots.example: The safe methods walk-through and the fitness to work form

safeMethods.body: Food safety here is the responsibility of {{food_safety_lead}}. Training held: {{staff_training}}. New staff receive {{induction}} and this is recorded on the training record before they handle food.
safeMethods.check: Before a new starter handles food, check the training record has their induction on it.
safeMethods.ifItGoesWrong: Do not let anyone handle food until the induction is done and recorded.
